failure: Spinal Fusion Device wear causing malfunction
constraint: Must maintain spinal fusion device function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Reduction of oxidative degradation and debris formation through refinement of polymeric components like ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene.
intervention: Apply cross-linked or vitamin-E-stabilized ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene bearing surfaces to the spinal fusion device's articulating components to minimize wear debris generation.
expected_effect: Decreased wear-induced osteolysis and debris accumulation, preserving device function within clinical specifications over extended implantation periods.
falsification_test: Conduct wear simulation testing per ASTM F1715 comparing conventional vs. refined UHMWPE spinal fusion articulating surfaces, measuring volumetric wear rate and particle size distribution; failure if refined material shows no significant reduction in wear debris or if device mechanical integrity degrades beyond ISO 18192-1 limits.
mechanism_source_span: "Polymeric components such as ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene has undergone significant refinement over the last several years leading to a reduction in oxidative degradation and debris formation."
